title: Glasgow surname and research-study newspaper records
scope: Pre-1800 review: 30 quoted given-name forms in Northern Ireland, including all 24 forms with documented historical catalogue occurrences; all 24 documented given-name forms in Ireland. All 71 Northern Ireland Glasgow entries (70 unique images), 18 Ireland Glasgow entries, ten Northern Ireland Glascow entries and sixteen Ireland Glasco entries were preview-screened. 178 catalogue targets include birth/tree leads as well as documented records. Original readings are separately labelled below. Earlier reviewed batches: The original 40 early pages (1690–1749), plus ten inspected pages selected for Montgreenan, Lisnagaver–Rasharkin and Larne–Kilwaughter studies. Wider searches covered 1690–1900, oldest first; large searches were sampled, not exhausted. A further locality batch searched Lisnagaver/Rasharkin spelling variants, named Glasgows and neighbouring places, chiefly 1690–1900 with selected later Lisnagaver checks through 1955; 54 selected result-page passages were read. Large searches were sampled; the curated catalogue adds only the two retained Daniel notices. The 4 October William batch loaded all 100 Northern Ireland exact-name result entries for 1690–1869 (98 unique pages), reviewed 71 saved search snippets, the supplied captures and selected original viewer passages. Eighteen curated surname pages were retained, including two later identity/family checks. This is not a claim that every passage on all 98 pages was read. An additional Ireland-country search returned 134 entries; its earliest inspected passage was a city false match and that corpus remains incomplete. A bounded 4 October coverage scan recorded worldwide Glasgow 1600–1899 (raw total 6,975,711; first page surveyed), Glasgow 1600–1749 (2,591; first ten surveyed), and fully loaded exact-name result sets for John, James, William, Hugh, Alexander, Andrew, Samuel, David, Adam, Thomas and George; only six newly inspected George vessel passages were added as exclusions. The pre-1900 Northern Ireland Benjamin query loaded all 157 result pages and saved all 166 thumbnail highlights. Root visually screened every highlight and fully read selected family notices. Full passage/identity review remains pending for 148 newly catalogued pages. A further original-page check resolves two early Andrew hits and the 1881 city match as exclusions, and retains the 1892 Jane Graham–Robert Glasgow death notice. Early Mary (seven), Margaret (ten) and Elizabeth (one) query sets also reached end of results. Nine newly catalogued Margaret pages are pending; additional query occurrences on existing pages are not presumed excluded by another passage’s city/vessel reading.
conclusion: The new early Irish evidence bridges the Dublin watchmaker’s 1779–1780 move from Christ-Church-lane to 20 Ormond Quay, without a first name or proved profile identity. William’s verified Rotterdam service now begins in April 1792. A worldwide John check adds a 1760 Nottingham store notice whose Irish origin is unproved. Repeated shipping and Kildress notices add sources, not new people or family links. The first early review retained James Glasgow’s 1740 shipping occurrence. Expanded study searches add nine surname pages and one separately labelled place record: Montgreenan family and estate notices, the original 1829 Lisnagaver freehold application, a Lisnagaver incident in 1861, and a Larne–Kilwaughter mill auction in 1804. A further locality search adds two appearances of Daniel Glasgow of Kilrea’s 1871 death notice: Church Street residence and an age of 73, conflicting with 75 in the civil register. No additional secure Alex/Robt occurrence at Lisnagaver was established in this bounded batch. The William review distinguishes the 1858 Cookstown witness uncle from co-plaintiff William, corroborates the Drapersfield partners, and strongly separates their Benjamin from Benjamin-2059 using a current July 1870 action. The original 1856 marriage confirms that Benjamin-2059 and his father John were Cookstown merchants. William-3814 is a strong candidate for the 1856 retired merchant; John’s parents remain unknown. The 1792 master, 1793 delegate and 1820 grocer are verified documentary roles with qualified household matches. Further original readings name Robert as the mill Benjamin’s father, add his 1864 Wilhelmina Pike marriage, and bridge Drapersfield to Hull through daughter Margaret George’s 1891 marriage. The separate Cookstown editor Henry’s 1897 notice supports existing family links; infant John’s 1857 notice recovers George as his middle name.
limitations: Inspected catalogue pages and retained surname pages are different counts. The place-study notice is not surname evidence.
The 1829 page is the original of a previously known derivative extract, not a second independent occurrence.
The newspaper marriage date is 22 February 1802; the maintained OPR citation gives 23 February. The 1835 appeal heading varies between reports.
Large keyword searches remain incomplete; OCR can join unrelated columns or miss a surname. No new founding-family connection or live WikiTree edit is claimed.
Licensed scans and reading captures remain private; stable original image links are published.

The 1871 Belfast death notices repeat one notice and are not independent confirmations of age. One attempted source download returned HTTP 429; that passage remains unread. Nearby surname hits without an established connection were not added to the local family account.

Certain documentary father–son relationship; identification of Robert with Glasgow-2656 or Glasgow-3941 remains qualified. Counsel’s reference to Robert’s sons supports a qualified brother inference for co-plaintiff William. The uncle’s paternal or maternal side and all mothers are unstated. No parents are established for John Glasgow-2058.
Cookstown notices lacking age or relatives are not automatically assigned to the uncle or younger partner.
Belfast News-Letter gives the Ohio elder’s age as 55; attributed Belfast Mercury gives 56. The 1875 Parsonstown notice is outside the pre-1870 window.
The supplied 1821 meeting signature and 1828 jury occurrence are James Glasgow, not William; the coffee agent is only B. Glasgow. Blank/duplicate crops do not add events.
Ireland-country results are separately indexed from Northern Ireland. The wider 134-entry result set and alternative OCR spellings have not been exhausted.

The 4 October worldwide and 1600–1749 coverage totals are raw search metadata with only the stated first page/first ten surveyed. Exact-name retrieval was complete for the listed queries, but passage inspection was partial for William, Andrew and Thomas; both outstanding Andrew IDs are now resolved as vessel/city passages. Nine newly catalogued Margaret pages remain pending original passage review; additional Margaret and Elizabeth matches on two existing pages remain uninspected. Same-name queries are not exhaustive surname coverage because OCR variants, women’s notices and non-English forms may be missed.

The revised pre-1800 pass screens first previews, not every match on every page. All sixteen Dublin watchmaker originals are now read and saved; they repeat one advertisement. Both Irish geographic collections and six older spellings were checked separately; quoted names alone miss line divisions and OCR variants. No completeness claim for pre-1800 people or pre-1900 newspapers is made.

rows.reading: At Dunlop-house, on the 22d ult. Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan, Esq. to Miss Rachel Dunlop, daughter of the late John Dunlop of Dunlop, Esq.
rows.assessment: The notice explicitly names Rachel’s father. Dunlop-2144 is a checked compatible John of Dunlop, whose biography lists Rachel’s 1769 baptism. Newspaper date is 22 February; the maintained OPR citation gives 23 February. Preserve both pending original-register comparison. No mother is stated.

rows.reading: Ayrshire list of game licences issued by the Sheriff’s Clerk between 12 July and 2 September 1802: Glasgow, Robert, Esq. of Montgreenan.
rows.assessment: Contemporary use of the estate designation by 2 September 1802. It supports the 1802 Montgreenan association, without dating the purchase or establishing a family relationship.

rows.reading: Game licences and deputations issued by the Sheriff Clerk of Ayrshire: Glasgow, Robert, Esq. of Montgreenan. A gamekeeper deputation also names Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan as principal.
rows.assessment: List covers 17 July–6 September 1806. Supports continued Montgreenan estate association; a deputation is an appointment of a gamekeeper, not kinship.

rows.reading: County of Ayr, Ayr, 13 January 1808: Robert Morris of Craig, for himself, and as authorised by Mr. Glasgow of Montgreenan.
rows.assessment: The county meeting debated trial by jury in civil cases. Montgreenan’s Glasgow was represented by an authorised attendee; this does not place him physically at the meeting. Name, estate and chronology fit Robert-1076.

rows.reading: At Rome, on the 22d ult. Mrs Robertson Glasgow, of Montgreenan, of a daughter.
rows.assessment: Reports a daughter born 22 November 1827 at Rome. Exact date, place and family designation support Charlotte Glasgow-3003’s recorded birth, but the notice does not give the child’s forename or the mother’s forename. Anne-2874 is the checked Montgreenan succession wife.

rows.reading: County of Antrim: List of Persons applying to Register their Freeholds, under 10 Geo. IV, cap. 8. No. 2324: Alex. Glasgow, Lisnagaver — Lands — Kilconway, townland of Lisnagaver.
rows.assessment: Original page now inspected; replaces the earlier access-blocked heading/extract assessment. This is an application, not proof of admission. No age or relative is stated. Alexander-951 and older Alexander-3904 remain compatible; conflicting age estimates prevent an automatic identification. The property is Lisnagaver; Kilconway is the barony.

rows.reading: Hugh Allan v. Trustees of Robert Glasgow: the report calls Mrs Robertson Glasgow the late Robert’s natural daughter and first heir under his 1818 entail. It reports his death in 1827 and a supplementary entail and trust dated 23 June 1821, involving Seafield near Ayr.
rows.assessment: Contemporary account of the 25 August hearing, independently supporting Anne’s daughter/heir description and the 1827 death year. It does not verify 19 April. Hugh Allan-8034, the profile-defined nephew, is a compatible appellant candidate; older Allan-8028 has no death recorded but would be 109. Neither identity is proved. These later deeds are distinct from the uninspected 1803 trust.

rows.reading: House of Lords appeals: the report reproduces clauses of Glasgow’s settlement and says Lord Brougham recommended reversing the judgment below; judgment reversed accordingly. The heading appears to read Henry Allen v. Trustees of R. Glasgow.
rows.assessment: Reports the Wednesday judgment, 2 September 1835. The estate, Seafield dispute and counsel identify the same litigation as the 26 August report, whose appellant is Hugh Allan. Preserve the discrepant heading; compare the original court papers before resolving the name. Reported deed extracts are not an inspection of the original deed.

rows.reading: Shocking catastrophe at Rasharkin: Robt. Glasgow, described as a neighbour at Lisnagaver, warned James M’Caughern about a dangerous gable before it fell; Glasgow narrowly escaped while leaving the doorway and raised the alarm.
rows.assessment: Genuine Glasgow surname in a local incident. Robert-938 and Robert-3449 remain compatible candidates; no age, parents, occupation or link to a valuation holding is stated. A later Scottish death does not exclude Robert-938 being in Ireland in 1861.

rows.reading: Auction advertised for 22 September at the Donegall Arms, Belfast: Larne corn and wheat mills, Kilwaughter corn mill, and Inver flour mills, with machinery, lands and lease interests in James Holmes & Co.’s possession.
rows.assessment: Place-study evidence only. Different mill interests were held under the heirs of the Marquis of Antrim and under the Marquis of Donegall. The passage names no Glasgow surname and does not connect the Glasgow families to these mills or to a seventeenth-century glassworks.
